summary: Quarterly renewal check-in focused on adding a short-term capacity uplift, onboarding an EU/APAC edge region, and negotiating a 12-month contract extension with staged committed capacity. Customer is leaning toward Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput but wants Private/VPC for EU data residency. Action: SOW, benchmark, security pack.
transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-10-08
- Start: 15:00 PDT
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Meeting recorded via Fireflies
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Nina (Redwood CSM), Elena (Northstar Head of ML), Jonas (Northstar CTO), Priya (Northstar Platform)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete): Discussed renewal, 3-month capacity addition, EU/APAC region onboarding, SOC2 docs, SOW timeline.

00:00 Elena: Okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for making time. We wanted to run through the renewal options and the capacity plan for the holiday peak in November.
00:18 Maya: Thanks Elena, yea, quick agenda from our side: review current usage, proposed uplift, region timeline for EU and APAC edge, and then sync on contract term. I'll hand over to Carlos for perf numbers.
00:32 Carlos: Hey all. Quick note, we've pulled the last 90 days of tokens and tail latencies; at our current Dedicated pool you're hitting about 250 tokens/s per GPU with 95th  latency at around 220ms for the production model. We expect with the 30% capacity bump you asked for that throughputs stays linear but we need to talk batching and KV cache hit rates.
00:54 Jonas: When you say KV cache hit rates, are you talking about prefix caching? We have a lot of repeated prompts from our routing logic.
01:07 Carlos: Exactly, prefix/K V cache — sometimes transcribed as K V cash — yes. If we configure the prefix cache on the staging pool we can halve token compute on repeated prompts. We also want to test the continuous batching window at your typical QPS.
01:22 Priya: For the EU region, regulatory team insists data at rest for EU customers stays in EU. We prefer private VPC deployment there. Is that available under Dedicated?
01:36 Maya: Short answer: yes. We can offer Redwood Dedicated in EU with a private control plane option — Redwood Private — so you get the VPC attachment and KMS in-region. There will be an uplift on pricing vs hosted.
01:51 Elena: What about onboarding time? We have roughly 6 weeks to get this provisioned before Black Friday-ish traffic and we want a guaranteed latency SLO.
02:03 Carlos: Typical Private/VPC onboarding is 3–5 weeks if network approvals go smoothly, longer if there are firewall/NAT egress policies. For latency SLOs, we can carve a dedicated pool with pinned GPUs and give a 99th percentile target; we'll show the historical traces in the benchmark.
02:25 Jonas: Are we locked into a 12-month commit if we take the Dedicated option? We want flexibility given uncertain volume after the holiday peak.
02:35 Maya: We recommend a staged commitment: a 3-month uplift on top of your existing contract to cover peak, then evaluate a 12-month extension with tiered committed capacity. That way you get predictability during peak without being forced into a long commitment immediately.
02:49 Elena: That sounds reasonable. Can you offer a break on price for the 12-month if we agree to the staged commit now?
03:00 Maya: Yes — we'll propose a tiered discount structure in the SOW. For example, 10% off list for a 12-month commit at current uplift, 5% off for a 6-month. We'll put clear breakpoints in the pricing table.
03:12 Priya: Regarding security, we need SOC2 Type II evidence, KMS integration instructions, and audit log retention for 2 years. Also SSO via SAML and RBAC scoping for our platform team.
03:27 Nina: We'll send the full security pack after this call — SOC2, penetration test summary, KMS patterns, and the RBAC mapping doc. We support SAML and can show sample SCIM mappings for automatic user provisioning.
03:45 Jonas: One question about cross-region failover. If EU Dedicated is down, can traffic fail over to US-hosted, or do you have a fallback to a reduced model? We cannot send production EU customer data to US.
03:58 Carlos: We can configure routing policies that default to EU Private; in case of region issue we can fail to a reduced capacity EU standby or to an EU-compatible hosted variant. We will not shift EU customer data to US unless you explicitly allow it. We'll also document the failover path in the runbook.
04:16 Elena: Okay good. Latency targets — our SREs want 95th < 250ms, 99th < 600ms with our current prompt length distribution. Can you meet that with quantized models?
04:30 Carlos: Yes, with optimized kernels and 8-bit quantization we can meet those latencies for the model family you're using; we need to test with your exact prompt mix. That's part of the benchmark plan.
04:42 Maya: On pricing, note that Private VPC has additional network and O&M costs. We'll show a per-token delta and a fixed monthly platform fee in the SOW.
04:53 Priya: Also we need to know egress costs and whether data residency controls have audit trails for compliance.
05:02 Nina: Audit logs are available via the console and can be exported to your SIEM; retention is configurable. We'll include sample exports in the security pack.
05:12 Elena: What's the timeline for the benchmark? We need results before we sign the SOW.
05:17 Carlos: We can run a 48–72 hour throughput and stability benchmark within 7 business days, assuming you share infra diagrams and the prompt set. It will include latency percentiles, GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rates.
05:31 Priya: I'll send the infra diagram and grant a test API key for staging tomorrow. Any constraints on how we run the tests?
05:38 Carlos: Provide a representative traffic replay and secrets redacted; we'll need an agreed QPS curve. We'll post prometheus endpoints and a dashboard link.
05:47 Maya: Next on contracts: we'll prepare two SOW options, one for Dedicated + Private EU for 3 months uplift then optional 12-month extension, and a hosted fallback proposal. We'll include price tables and lead times.
06:00 Jonas: If we sign the 3-month uplift, do you guarantee capacity during the peak or is it best-effort?
06:09 Maya: For reserved capacity we guarantee throughput in the service-level section. For the short uplift we can carve out reserved GPU pool and include an SLA for provisioning time and latency targets.
06:20 Elena: Any competitors you see as higher risk during procurement? We are talking to Bedrock and evaluating self-hosted Triton prototypes.
06:29 Carlos: Bedrock is convenient but the pricing model can be opaque. Self-hosting gives maximum control but comes with ops burden and unpredictable kernel-level performance. We'll include a cost-per-1M token comparison in the SOW.
06:44 Priya: Ok. A couple of small asks: can you support our KMS provider (Azure Key Vault) in EU region, and can you supply IAM roles for read-only dashboards?
06:55 Nina: We integrate with Azure Key Vault for customer-managed keys in region. And we can provision read-only dashboards via IAM mapping; we'll include a sample policy.
07:06 Maya: Great. To recap: Redwood action items are SOW draft with tiered pricing (Maya), benchmark plan + dashboard (Carlos), security pack (Nina). Northstar will share infra diagram, prompt set, and constraints (Priya). We'll aim to have the SOW and benchmark plan by next week.
07:28 Elena: That works. Any open questions?
07:31 Jonas: No, other than timeline — please make sure the SOW lists explicit provisioning windows so procurement can sign off.
07:38 Maya: Will do.
07:40 Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and set the onboarding call once the SOW is accepted.
07:46 Elena: Thanks — talk soon.

End of transcript.
